metaTitle: Best Furniture Anti Tip Kits in 2026
metaDescription: Six furniture anti tip kits compared on strap material, load rating, wall fit and install effort, so dressers, bookcases and TV stands stay upright.
expertTake: The Hangman TK-400 is the top pick because its galvanized steel cable and 400 pound rating suit dressers and TV stands. The AXYLOEVA 12 pack is the value pick for a whole house. Skip adhesive kits for tall or loaded pieces, because they rely on the wall surface rather than a stud.
introParagraphs: Tall dressers, bookcases and TV stands can tip when a child climbs a drawer or an earthquake shakes the wall. An anti tip kit ties the piece to the wall so a sudden shift does not become a fall.
A kit is only as strong as the strap, the hardware and the wall anchor. Buyers should look at material, load rating, how the strap attaches and whether the wall is drywall, plaster or masonry.

products.name: Hangman TK-400 Anti Tip Kit, Steel Cable, 400 lb
products.description:
Hangman's TK-400 is built from galvanized aircraft steel cable and steel components, and it carries a 400 pound rating. The listing says it works for dressers, filing cabinets and full length mirrors. Steel cable does not stretch the way fabric does, which is a real advantage when a tall piece leans forward under a child's weight.

Compared with the plastic and fabric strap kits, the TK-400 feels like proper hardware. One kit secures one piece, so a bedroom with three dressers needs three kits or a multi pack. That is a cost to plan for, but it also means every piece gets a full set of hardware rather than a shared allotment.

Install it with a stud finder and a drill. Fasten the wall plate into a stud and the furniture plate into the frame, never the thin back panel, which can pull through. A level and a pencil make the job quick, and the cable should be snug but not bowstring tight so that the furniture can still be slid out for cleaning. It is the safest everyday choice for a tall dresser.
products.bestFor: Tall dressers, TV stands and mirrors that need a rated steel strap.
pros: Galvanized steel cable does not stretch
cons: Needs a stud finder and drill

products.name: PUTORSEN Heavy Duty Anti Tip Anchors, 4 Sets, 500 lb
products.description:
PUTORSEN lists a 500 pound capacity across four adjustable sets with thickened solid metal bodies. The listing describes a one click buckle that installs in three steps, and the quick release lets you detach the furniture to clean or move it without taking the wall hardware out. That makes it the highest rated kit in this guide.

Quick release is the real strength. Households move furniture for cleaning and rearranging, and a strap that opens easily is more likely to be reconnected. The cost is that any buckle can also be opened by a determined child, so mount the strap high and behind the piece where little hands cannot reach it.

Compared with the Hangman TK-400, you get four sets instead of one and a different attachment design. Make sure the wall anchor goes into a stud and that the strap is snug but not overtight. For a tall bookcase or a heavy TV stand, the higher rating is a useful margin, and the four sets cover the most common bedroom or living room load.
products.bestFor: Heavy bookcases and tall furniture that you may need to move.
cons: Buckle adds a part that could be released by accident

products.name: HOME MASTER HARDWARE Anti Tip Straps for Dressers, 4 Pack, 400 lb
products.description:
HOME MASTER HARDWARE sells four steel straps with a 400 pound load capacity, aimed at dressers and kitchen or bathroom cabinets. A four pack covers a bedroom with two dressers and a bookcase, which is the usual set of pieces in a child's room.

The steel strap resists stretching, and the kit includes hardware for both the wall and the furniture. That matches the Hangman TK-400 on the rating, and it gives you four pieces for the job of one. The tradeoff is less brand documentation, so read the supplied instructions carefully.

Install into studs where possible and use the supplied screws, not drywall anchors alone. The straps are visible against the back of a dresser, but they are small and easy to hide behind decor. For baby proofing a whole room on a single order, it is the simplest steel option here. If your dresser is deep, check that the strap length reaches the stud without pulling the piece away from the wall.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms with several dressers and cabinets.

products.name: AXYLOEVA Steel Anti Tip Furniture Anchors, 12 Pack
products.description:
AXYLOEVA supplies 12 reinforced steel anchors in a single pack, which makes it the best coverage for a whole house. The listing describes expansion tubes and screws, and a simple mark, drill and install process. The finish is described as rust resistant and the listing says it outlasts plastic anchors.

Steel hardware holds up better than plastic over years, and the expansion tubes grip drywall when a stud is not available. That is not the same as a stud, which is the strongest possible hold, so use the studs when you can and the tubes only where a stud is not behind the piece. Plan a few minutes per piece.

Compared with the Hangman, you get many more anchors but less documented capacity, so it suits a family with lots of mid weight furniture rather than one very heavy piece. Check each anchor after a month. It is the smart pick for a family that wants every dresser, bookcase and cabinet secured on one order. Mark the stud height on a piece of painter's tape first, and every anchor lines up quickly.
products.bestFor: Whole house coverage of many pieces.
cons: Expansion tubes are weaker than studs

products.name: Smloplom Anti Tip Furniture Anchors, 12 Pack, 450 lb
products.description:
Smloplom lists 12 steel anchors with a 450 pound rating, finished in white. White hardware blends with painted walls and light furniture, which matters in a nursery or a bedroom where the strap will always be visible.

The rating sits between the Hangman at 400 pounds and the PUTORSEN at 500 pounds, and a 12 pack covers a family home. Compared with the AXYLOEVA, it publishes a rating, which gives you a number to compare. It also offers a whole house count at a similar tier.

Install with studs where possible and follow the screw and anchor instructions. The rating is only as good as the wall and the screws, so do not skip the stud finder. For a family that wants clear numbers, a large count and a neat look, it is a strong middle choice.
products.bestFor: Whole house with a stated rating and a white finish.

products.name: AccEncyc No Drill Adhesive Anti Tip Kit, 6 Pack
products.description:
AccEncyc is the no drill option. Self adhesive pads and an adjustable L bracket attach to the wall without holes, which suits renters and anyone whose lease forbids drilling. A six pack covers a few pieces.

Adhesive hold depends on a clean, smooth, well bonded wall, and textured or freshly painted surfaces can be unreliable. It is best for lighter pieces and for supplementing, not replacing, a steel kit on a tall or loaded dresser. Do not use it on a heavy, tall bookcase.

Compared with the steel kits above, it trades strength for convenience. Clean the wall with rubbing alcohol, let the pads cure for the time the instructions state and keep the bracket snug. Use it where drilling is not allowed and the furniture is modest.
products.bestFor: Renters and lighter furniture where drilling is not allowed.
cons: Adhesive hold depends on the wall
Not for heavy or tall pieces

buyingCriteria.explanation: Steel cable or strap, as on the Hangman and HOME MASTER, does not stretch under load. Fabric and plastic straps can fray, stretch and fail over years of daily use. If a kit uses nylon, check that it is thick and rated, and replace it if it looks worn. A material that gives under load defeats the point of the kit. Check that cable crimps and buckles are metal, because a plastic buckle can crack in cold rooms.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Load rating and what it means
buyingCriteria.explanation: Ratings in this group run from 400 to 500 pounds, with the PUTORSEN at 500, the Smloplom at 450 and the Hangman at 400. Those numbers assume the anchor goes into a stud with the supplied screws. A rating is not a guarantee in a weak wall, so treat it as a ceiling. A filled dresser with drawers pulled can exert more force than its resting weight.

Drywall needs studs or toggle anchors, plaster needs a masonry bit and patience, and concrete needs masonry anchors. The AXYLOEVA includes expansion tubes for drywall, which are fine as a backup. Before you buy, tap the wall to find studs and check your wall type. The common mistake is mounting into drywall alone and trusting a plastic anchor. A magnetic stud finder tracks the drywall screws and gives a reliable guide in older homes.

Count your pieces before shopping. A tall dresser needs one or two straps, a bookcase needs two and a TV stand needs one or two. The AXYLOEVA and Smloplom each include 12, while the Hangman covers one piece per kit. Buy a few extra for items you plan to add. Heavy, wide pieces such as a 60 inch dresser benefit from two straps spaced apart rather than one in the center.

A quick release buckle, like the PUTORSEN's, lets you move furniture without removing the wall hardware. A fixed strap is more secure but harder to remove. If you vacuum behind furniture often, quick release is the better daily design. Make sure the release cannot be opened by a child.

Adhesive kits like the AccEncyc avoid holes but rely on the wall surface and the bond. Screws into studs give the strongest hold. Use adhesive only for light pieces or in rentals, and never rely on it for a tall, loaded dresser. Check the bond after a week and a month.

howWeEvaluated.title: Strength and material
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared strap materials, ratings and hardware. The PUTORSEN at 500 pounds and the Hangman's galvanized steel cable lead the group. A kit that stretches or uses weak metal scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wall compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the anchors and adhesives supplied. The AXYLOEVA's expansion tubes and the AccEncyc's pads serve different walls. A kit that includes the right hardware for common walls scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install effort
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed the number of steps and tools needed. The PUTORSEN lists a three step install, and the Hangman needs a drill and a stud finder. Easier installs are more likely to be completed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Coverage and count
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how many pieces a pack secures. The AXYLOEVA and Smloplom offer 12 each, while the Hangman secures one. A pack that matches a typical home scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at removal, reuse and visibility. Quick release helps in homes that rearrange. Owner feedback patterns informed our advice to recheck straps after a few months.

cards.label: Steel
cards.text: The Hangman, PUTORSEN, HOME MASTER, AXYLOEVA and Smloplom screw into the wall and resist stretching. They give the strongest hold, especially into studs, and they last for years.

cards.label: Adhesive
cards.text: The AccEncyc avoids holes and suits renters, but it relies on the wall surface and the bond. It is best for light pieces or as a backup.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Steel straps, stud installation and a strap placed high and behind the piece. Avoid fabric straps that can fray and buckles that a child can open. Anchor every tall piece in a child's room.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Hangman TK-400 and HOME MASTER four pack fit best, with the PUTORSEN as the choice for heavy bookcases. Skip the AccEncyc for tall dressers.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your furniture is heavy or tall, such as a filled bookcase. The PUTORSEN at 500 pounds and the Hangman's steel cable justify a higher tier.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your pieces are modest and you need many anchors. The AXYLOEVA and Smloplom 12 packs cover a whole home at a lower tier.

maintenance.why: Straps loosen as furniture moves. A snug strap resists a sudden tip.
Screws loosen with vibration and use. Tighten them so the anchor does not pull out.
Adhesive can weaken with heat and humidity. Replace pads that lift.
A strap left off is no protection. Make reattaching part of cleaning.
Anchors can loosen if the wall cracks. Repair the wall and reinstall.

faq.q: Do I need to find studs for an anti tip kit?
faq.a: Studs give the strongest hold and are the recommended anchor point for any tall or heavy piece. A stud finder takes a minute and saves a lot of risk. If no stud is behind the piece, use expansion tubes or toggle anchors rated for the load. Mark each stud edge with tape before drilling, and drill the pilot hole in the center of the stud.

faq.q: Are adhesive anti tip kits safe?
faq.a: They are suitable for light pieces on smooth, clean walls and for renters who cannot drill. They are not a good choice for a tall, loaded dresser or a heavy bookcase. Treat them as a backup and check the bond regularly.

faq.q: How many straps does one piece need?
faq.a: A tall dresser or bookcase should have two straps, one near each side of the top. A short TV stand may need one. Use more for wide pieces, because a single strap can let one side lift. Wide dressers and bookcases with a deep top overhang need straps at both ends so the piece cannot pivot.

faq.q: Will an anti tip kit damage my walls?
faq.a: It leaves small screw holes that can be patched with spackle when you remove it. Adhesive kits can lift paint if removed carelessly. Warm the pad gently and peel slowly.

faq.q: Can I use an anti tip kit on a TV stand?
faq.a: Yes. Anchor the stand or console to the wall and consider a second strap for the TV itself. Make sure the screws go into a sturdy part of the frame, not a thin back panel.

faq.q: How tight should the strap be?
faq.a: The strap should be snug with little slack, but not so tight that it bows the furniture. A small amount of play helps when you slide the piece out for cleaning. Recheck after a few weeks. If a strap has to be loosened to move the piece, retighten it when you push the furniture back.
